newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Single-digit growth seen for SHK Properties profit.
newsitem.headline: Single-digit growth seen for SHK Properties profit.

text.p: Slow industrial property sales are likely to have hampered earnings growth at Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd in the 1995/96 financial year and analysts said they expect only single-digit profit growth during the period.
The property investment and development company is due to report its results for the year to June 30, 1996, on Wednesday.
"The earnings (growth) will be around six to seven percent and that is mainly because the booking of industrial office profit is not that satisfactory," said Henry Kwong, analyst at Merrill Lynch.
Sun Hung Kai Properties posted 1994/95 net profit of HK$10.36 billion (US$1.33 billion). During the six months ended December 31, 1995, the company reported net profit of HK$5.15 billion.

David Low, research manager at Asia Equity, said he expected net profit growth of seven percent, and in view of the slow industrial property sector, 1995/96 was a "decent" year for Sun Hung Kai Properties.

"They actually had more industrial property projects in financial year 1996 and despite that they managed to get seven percent growth. They had as much of 20 percent of profits coming from the industrial side and they managed to sell quite a lot of those," he said.
Franklin Lam, director of research at HG Asia, said 1995/96 was a low period for the company.
"This will mark the lowest year of earnings growth for Sun Hung Kai Properties for quite a while. In terms of volume sales, last year was a low period for Sun Hung Kai Properties," he said.

Lam forecast net profit of HK$11.19 billion. "The margins and everything are actually lower in 1996 because the bulk of sales was related to transactions achieved in the second half of 1995, which was the one of the lowest transaction periods we have seen in Hong Kong in the last six years," he said.
Being a big volume seller, Sun Hung Kai Properties would have been affected more than other property developers by the slow sales in the second half of 1995, Lam said.

"It will hit Sun Hung Kai Properties in the trading up that the company specialises in," he said, adding that bulk of the company's supply was aimed at buyers trading in existing homes for more expensive premises.
"I think property sales are quite flat," added Asia Equity's Low. But he said the results announcement should be a non-event and earnings were set to improve.
"They have been very transparent so there should not be many surprises. Looking ahead it should be very much a different picture," he said.
Low said Sun Hung Kai Properties is expected to have more residential projects and benefit from increases in prices.

"In terms of the coming year, we expect growth of 14 percent mainly due to contributions from the pre-sales of Royal Ascot Two and East Point City," said Dennis Leung, analyst at Dharmala Securities. He expected 1995/96 net profit of HK$11.3 billion.
Sun Hung Kai Properties shares rose to an all-time high on Monday of HK$82.50, up HK$1.75, before ending the day at HK$82.25.
